reviews.body: Thanks for the PR! Main request here is to fix the same issue in a few other places where it pops up (see in-line comments)

review_comments.body:
The same bug exists in six other constructors, all reading the credential as `api_config.get(...) if api_config else os.getenv(...)`. With the env var set and an `api_config` that lacks the credential, each raises instead of using the env:
- `utils/vectorize/text/cohere.py:153`
- `utils/vectorize/text/mistral.py:134`
- `utils/vectorize/voyageai.py:281`
- `utils/vectorize/vertexai.py:185` and `:188` (`project_id` and `location`; for example, passing only `credentials` ignores `GCP_PROJECT_ID`)
- `utils/rerank/cohere.py:91`
- `utils/rerank/voyageai.py:90`

Since the PR describes the pattern rather than one provider, please apply the same per-key fallback (`api_config.get(key) or os.getenv(ENV)`) to each of these, with one parametrised regression test across them. These siblings use `get` and don't forward the rest of `api_config`, so they don't need the copy-and-`pop` that OpenAI and Azure do.

With this change an `api_key` of `""` or `None` in `api_config` falls back to `OPENAI_API_KEY`; on main it raised `ValueError`. That matches Azure and suits MCP YAML such as `${OPENAI_API_KEY:-}`, but it's a behaviour change. Please say in the `api_config` docstring of `__init__` (line 83) that each key falls back to its environment variable when missing or empty, and mention it in the Release Notes.

Nothing here builds `OpenAITextVectorizer()` without an `api_config`, which is the default and most common path. Changing `dict(api_config or {})` to `dict(api_config)` crashes on `None`, yet all four tests still pass. Please add an env-only test like `test_init_from_env_vars_configures_both_clients` in `tests/unit/test_azure_openai_vectorizer.py`. A case with `{"api_key": ""}` falling back to the env would pin the behaviour change above too.
`_Item`, `_Response` and `_Embeddings` can be `types.SimpleNamespace` objects, as in `tests/unit/test_cohere_vectorizer.py:18`, which removes about 15 lines of scaffolding.

The last column of `CASES` (the fake package) is never read, and `key` is `"api_key"` in every row. Dropping both and defining the decorator once, e.g. `SIBLINGS = pytest.mark.parametrize("module_name,class_name,env", [c[1:4] for c in CASES], ids=[c[0] for c in CASES])`, and then using `@SIBLINGS` on all three tests, removes the unused `key, _pkg` parameters and about 15 lines.

comments.body:
Applied in d299a66:
- Sibling constructors: per-key `(api_config or {}).get(k) or os.getenv(ENV)` at all six listed sites, VertexAI for both `project_id` and `location`, with one parametrised regression test in `tests/unit/test_api_config_env_fallback.py`. `None` is kept in the expression because `api_config` defaults to it on the paths that do not normalise it first.
- Behaviour change: the `api_config` docstrings now state the fallback for missing or empty keys, and the PR description's Release Notes mention it.
- OpenAI tests: added an env-only test and `""`/`None` `api_key` cases.
- Scaffolding: `_Item` and `_Response` are now `SimpleNamespace`; `_Embeddings` stays a class because it has a `create` method.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
I can get this PR merged as soon as that last comment is addressed 🙌

Applied in 7f061f7: dropped the unused `key`/fake-package columns from `CASES` and defined the decorator once as `SIBLINGS`, used on all three tests (the config key is the literal `"api_key"` in the one test that needs it).

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
